qs.q: A major part of gallbladder contractions are due to:
o: Vagal stimulation together with cholecystokinin (CCK) drives gallbladder contraction.
Gastrin is the main stimulus for gallbladder contraction.
qs.e: Gallbladder contraction is primarily stimulated by Cholecystokinin (CCK), released in response to fats and proteins in the duodenum. Vagal (parasympathetic) stimulation also contributes to gallbladder contraction. Secretin primarily stimulates bicarbonate secretion. Gastrin stimulates gastric acid. Somatostatin is inhibitory.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - August 21, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which feature is NOT part of virilism in women? ---
qs.e: Galactorrhea is related to hyperprolactinemia, whereas virilism involves manifestations like temporal recession, clitoromegaly, and voice deepening.

qs.q: Which factor is NOT part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway? ---
qs.e: Factor VII belongs to the tissue-factor (extrinsic) pathway rather than the intrinsic pathway.

qs.q: Citric acid cycle is part of what metabolic pathway? ---
qs.e: The citric acid cycle is amphibolic because it functions in both catabolic and anabolic processes.

qs.q: Which part of the Loop of Henle is more permeable to water? ---
qs.e: The distal convoluted tubule has fewer microvilli than the proximal tubule and performs regulated solute transport, including NaCl reabsorption and calcium handling.
qs.s: END YEAR PP1 & PP2 2025 Physiology: MCQs for Medical School Exams

qs.q: Which part of the renal tubule has fewer microvilli and its main function is secretion? ---
qs.e: Macula densa cells sense tubular NaCl delivery and signal to nearby juxtaglomerular cells and vascular structures. They are specialized epithelial cells of the distal tubule.
qs.s: END YEAR PP1 & PP2 2025 Physiology: MCQs for Medical School Exams

qs.q: Which microorganism can be part of normal vaginal flora and cause meningitis in newborns?
qs.e: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Strep) is normal vaginal flora in ~25% of women but can cause serious infections in newborns, including meningitis, pneumonia, and sepsis.
qs.s: Medical Bacteriology and Entomology Exam 2020/2021 MCQs

qs.q: Most ventricular septal defects (VSDs) occur in which part of the septum?
qs.e: The membranous part of the ventricular septum is the most common site for VSDs.

es.q: As part of a forensic investigation involving a suspected poisoning, the role of the liver in metabolism and excretion is crucial. Outline the primary functions of bile in the human body.
es.m: Bile plays two primary functions essential for bodily health: 1. **Elimination:** It facilitates the excretion of water-insoluble substances, including bilirubin, excess cholesterol, and various xenobiotics (foreign compounds) from the body. 2. **Emulsification:** In the gut, bile emulsifies dietary fats, a critical step for their digestion and absorption.
